title: Influence of feedpowder morphology on microstructure and mechanical properties of Tantalum produced by cold spray additive manufacturing
InformationInFigures: Yes. nozzle type, deposit dimensions, tensile dimensions (Fig. 1), D-values for PSD (Fig. 2), type of grains in deposit (Fig. 6)

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: polygonal, with smooth surface with a well-dispersed particle distribution, lacking significant agglomeration or adsorption. 530 ppm oxygen content.
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: polished with 800-grit sandpaper to remove the surface oxide layers and subsequently cleaned ultrasonically in acetone.

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: Prior to testing, the samples were polished with 800 μm sandpaper to remove the oxide layer and heat-affected zone caused by wire cutting. The test sample size was 10 mm × 10 mm × 3 mm, and three samples were tested

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: particles are compressed and stacked due to plastic deformation, tightly bound and filling the particle interface. dense deposit, 16.56 ± 0.03 g/cm^3. particle-particle interface has fine grain region, elongated grain region away from particle-particle interface, and coarse grain region at the particle center. 60.6% high-angle grain boundaries. mostly deformed grains (~70%), some structured grains (~20%), some recrystallized grains (<10%). stronger mechanical interlocking.

Experiments.Notes: A-Ta powder, Ta-1 deposit. With a nanoindenter load of 50 mN and same hold time, the nanohardness value was 3.34 ± 0.23 GPa and the EM was 210.1 ± 12 GPa

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: particles are compressed and stacked due to plastic deformation, but retains numerous pits at the surface caused by shot peening, indicating the rebounding of particles. a metal jet observed between powders due to high strain rate.  dense deposit, 16.50 ± 0.04 g/cm^3, small amount of porosity. particle-particle interface has fine grain region, elongated grain region away from particle-particle interface, and coarse grain region at the particle center. 55.2% high-angle grain boundaries. Mostly deformed grains (>50%), some structured grains (~35%), few recrystallized grains (~5%).
